> Download a PRIDE project's files, all of them or a selection, into a directory and report the paths written.

Wire verb `pride download` · Python [`pymzlib.pride.download`][pymzlib.pride.download]

### Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default | Unit | Range | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `accession` | `string` | required | — | — | The project accession, e.g. PXD000001. The bridge checks only that it is not blank. |
| `dest` | `path` | required | — | — | Directory to write into; created if absent, but only when a file is actually fetched (mzLib creates it after the no-overwrite skip). With zero matches, or every file skipped, no directory is created, yet destination_directory is still reported. Blank is a usage error (it never falls back to the working directory). |
| `category` | `string` | absent | — | `a PRIDE category value, case-insensitive: RAW, PEAK, SEARCH, RESULT, OTHER, ...` | Keep only files of this category (mzLib WhereCategory). Absent keeps every category. Given but blank is a usage error, never 'everything'. ANDed with ext. |
| `ext` | `string[]` | absent | — | `comma-separated; a leading dot is optional` | Keep only files whose name ends with one of these extensions, case-insensitive (mzLib WhereExtension), e.g. ".raw,.mzML". Absent keeps every type. Given but naming no extension (blank or only commas) is a usage error. A compressed file's extension is .gz. |
| `no_overwrite` (wire `--no-overwrite`) | `flag` | `false` | — | — | Leave a file already present at the destination untouched and make no request for it: a cheap resume. Absent, an existing file is replaced. |
| `names_from_stdin` (wire `--names-from-stdin`) | `flag` | `false` | — | — | Select exact files instead of filtering: stdin carries file names, one per line (newline-delimited; blank lines ignored; each line trimmed; exact, case-sensitive match against the manifest's file_name). Exclusive with category and ext. Stdin rather than argv because argv caps near 32 KB and any other separator could occur in a file name. A name containing a line break cannot be selected (the bindings refuse one; PRIDE has never published one). |
| `stdin` | `string[]` | absent | — | `>= 1 non-blank line when names-from-stdin is given` | Read only with names-from-stdin: the file names to fetch, one per line. Every name must be in the project's REST manifest (pride files). A UTF-8 BOM on the first line is stripped (ReadStdinLines) from pyMzLib #67 on; the 0.2.0 bridge keeps it, so that first name fails as not in the project. |

### Returns

Top-level fields:

| Field | Type | Unit | Null? | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `accession` | `string` | — | never | The accession, echoed as given. |
| `destination_directory` | `string` | — | never | dest, made absolute. |
| `downloaded_count` | `int` | files | never | Entries in paths: files written PLUS, under no-overwrite, files already present and skipped. |
| `paths` | `string[]` | — | never | One path per selected file, in manifest order: mzLib's Path.Combine(dest as given, file_name), so relative when dest was relative (resolve against destination_directory's parent, not this list). |

### Errors

| Kind | pyMzLib raises | When |
|---|---|---|
| `usage` | [`UsageError`][pymzlib.UsageError] | accession or dest missing or blank; category given but blank; ext given but naming no extension; names-from-stdin together with category or ext; names-from-stdin with no non-blank line on stdin |
| `usage` | [`UsageError`][pymzlib.UsageError] | names-from-stdin naming a file the project's manifest does not contain (the message lists up to five). Raised AFTER the matching files have been downloaded: they are on disk when the error arrives. |
| `service_unavailable` | [`ServiceUnavailableError`][pymzlib.ServiceUnavailableError] | the bridge's own classification (Program.ClassifyError; since mzLib 1.0.593 (#1350) PRIDE raises every transport failure as an HttpRequestException carrying the cause or the status, and messages name the file and host, never the URL): a timeout, a socket or TLS failure, an HTTP 408, 429 or 5xx on the manifest or a file, a body that delivered nothing for mzLib's BodyStallTimeout (2 min), or a body cut off in transit |
| `correctness` | [`BridgeError`][pymzlib.BridgeError] | a selected file has no HTTPS location (NotSupportedException; Aspera-only); a manifest file name that is not a bare leaf name (ArgumentException: refusing to write outside dest); any other HTTP status; a local disk failure while writing (a bare IOException, e.g. a full disk, is deliberately NOT treated as an outage); a 403 from ftp.pride.ebi.ac.uk after mzLib's retries (mzLib retries it as EBI's rate limit, but the bridge classifies by status, so it crosses as correctness; PRIDE-B3 asks mzLib to mark such failures) |

### Caveats

- Since mzLib 1.0.594 (#1412), PrideArchiveClient retries a transient failure, that request alone, after 5, 20 and 60 s (a 429 or 503 Retry-After of up to 60 s replaces the wait); transient means no HTTP status at all, 408, 429, any 5xx, or a 403 from ftp.pride.ebi.ac.uk, EBI's rate limit. Each attempt can take up to the client's 100 s timeout, so a service that hangs takes up to about 485 s per request before the failure is reported. A binding's own timeout shorter than that reports a hanging outage as a timeout, not as service_unavailable.
- Selects from PRIDE's REST manifest (pride files), which omits some files; a file listed only by pride ftp-files cannot be downloaded by this verb.
- Files are fetched one at a time, in manifest order. Each streams to '<name>.partial' and is moved into place only when complete, so an interrupted transfer never leaves a truncated file under its final name; files finished before a failure stay on disk. Since mzLib 1.0.594 (#1412), a transfer that fails after its retries leaves '<name>.partial' and '<name>.partial.validator' in dest on purpose: the next call resumes from them. dest can therefore hold these pairs after a failed call.
- No size, MD5 or EBI error-page check reaches this verb. mzLib 1.0.595 verifies a download against PRIDE's checksums and the announced size, and scans a small body for EBI's error text (#1427, #1449: on 2026-10-07 and 08 about 23 of about 70 large transfers came back at the right size holding an error page), but only on the DownloadFileAsync overload that takes a PrideFileChecksum. DownloadProjectFilesAsync, which this verb calls, uses the overload without one, so such a file is reported as downloaded. Verify large files yourself, against the size and MD5 pride checksums lists, until the bridge can ask for the check.
- A filter that matches nothing, or an unknown accession, succeeds with downloaded_count 0 on the wire. The bindings raise a usage error when a category or ext filter matched nothing.
- Downloads can be very large (PXD000001's single .raw is about 220 MB); list first and filter or select.

!!! warning "Not yet verified"

    - No recorded fixture, so no checked example: a replay needs a stub bridge that also fakes the written files. The envelope keys above are read from the object PrideDownloadAsync returns, not from a recording.
    - The unmatched-selection check runs after the download, so a typo in one name still downloads every other selected file before failing. Checking the manifest first would need the bridge to fetch it separately from DownloadProjectFilesAsync.
    - A zero-match filter is a usage error in the bindings but a success on the wire; whether the wire should raise it (as it does for an unmatched names-from-stdin selection) is undecided.
